symptom_short: A client connected to a non-leader quorum member issues a create-with-stat write; the request is never answered, the member's commit pipeline halts, and every client on that member is disconnected

milestones.note: Folder scaffolded (private/ source/ logs/ diagnosis/); PROGRESS.md + state.json created; bug claimed in COORDINATION.log.

JIRA ZOOKEEPER-1851 ('Follower and Observer Request Processors Do Not Forward create2 Requests', Blocker, affects+fixVersion 3.5.0, Resolved/Fixed). Fix commit = bcf09c846 (Rakesh Radhakrishnan, 2014-07-18, svn trunk@1611732). Its diff adds the missing 'case OpCode.create2:' to (1) FollowerRequestProcessor.run's forward-to-leader switch, (2) ObserverRequestProcessor.run's forward-to-leader switch, (3) CommitProcessor.needCommit(), and (4) TraceFormatter.op2String (log/trace only); it also adds test QuorumRequestPipelineTest + QuorumBase refactor. pre_fix_commit = 25ea38a87 (ZOOKEEPER-1968, last commit where the bug exists; verified its FollowerRequestProcessor switch has create/delete/setData/reconfig/setACL/multi/check but NOT create2). Confirmed the diff resolves the reported symptom: without the case, the follower queues the request into CommitProcessor but never ships it to the leader; needCommit()==false makes CommitProcessor treat it as a read and hand it to FinalRequestProcessor with request.getHdr()==null, where the isQuorum() branch calls ZKDatabase.addCommittedProposal -> request.getHdr().serialize() -> NPE outside the processor's try/catch; WorkerService then runs CommitWorkRequest.cleanup(), which halts the CommitProcessor, so the member answers nothing further and its clients are disconnected.

Built the pre-fix tree (25ea38a87, ZooKeeper 3.5.0-SNAPSHOT) from source with Ant+Ivy in per-bug image clods-eval:Zookeeper-Zookeeper-1851 (clods-eval + openjdk-8-jdk + ant; JDK11/17 refuse -source/-target<7). Build cmd: 'ant jar' -> build/zookeeper-3.5.0-SNAPSHOT.jar + build/classes + build/lib (slf4j 1.7.5, log4j 1.2.16, jline 2.11, netty 3.7.0.Final, jetty 6.1.26, jackson 1.9.11, commons-cli 1.2). Dep fixes (private/deps-fix.patch, 3 edits, no source changes): (1) build.xml ivy.url http://repo2.maven.org -> https://repo1.maven.org (repo2 host is gone and Central refuses plain HTTP); (2) build.xml javac.source/javac.target 1.5 -> 1.8 (javac 8 rejects source/target 1.5 pairing with its 1.8 default bootclasspath); (3) ivysettings.xml repo.maven.org/repo.jboss.org/repo.sun.org -> https://repo1.maven.org (jboss + download.java.net are dead). BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 10s.

REDONE under the updated methodology (two logs + production merge + neutral repro naming). Neutral naming: the previous run's znode path /app/failing/with-stat and the client_failing.log collection header named both the failing session and the at-fault operation inside an LLM-facing artifact; paths are now /app/svcN/item-9137 + /app/cfg-N, workloads are c1..c4, and collection headers follow the production log's own host__path convention (zk11.., app5..). Reproduced again on the real 3-node ensemble (leader 24553/myid3, followers 24551/myid1 + 24552/myid2): plain create OK 8ms, create-with-Stat ConnectionLoss, node absent, follower's pipeline dead, collateral client 20 ok then 5 ConnectionLoss. Log A = private/symptom.orig.log, 19049 lines. Log B = private/merged.orig.log, 8068887 lines / 1.5GB = Log A merged into the shared read-only production-logs/Zookeeper/production.log (8052741 records, 2026-08-14 18:44-19:32, YCSB+chaos). MERGE DEVIATION (documented in reproduce.md): the spec's literal timestamp merge assumes a globally sorted production log, but this one is 10 concatenated per-host sections each restarting the clock over the same window, so a timestamp merge collapsed 80% of the reproduction into the first 500k of 8.07M lines - one contiguous foreign block, exactly what the methodology forbids. private/merge_logs.py keeps the specified retiming (linear warp preserving relative order and gaps) and changes only the interleaving key to proportional record position (--interleave position; --interleave timestamp still implements the literal rule). Reproduction is now spread across all 10 sections (per 1M lines: 820/509/379/18/62/0/0/1512/93). Findability: 'Client session timed out' 10 hits, 'NullPointerException' 1, 'unable to continue' 1.

Type renames (file + public type + every reference, so log tags and stack frames follow): FollowerRequestProcessor->FollowerIngressProcessor, ObserverRequestProcessor->ObserverIngressProcessor, CommitProcessor->StagedRequestProcessor (+ inner CommitWorkRequest->StageWorkRequest and the 20 lower-case field spellings), FinalRequestProcessor->TerminalRequestProcessor, ZKDatabase->ZKStateStore (+ zkDatabase/zkdatabase spellings incl. 9 javadoc occurrences), WorkerService->TaskExecutorPool, TraceFormatter->OpNameFormatter. Log-statement rewrites: 'Processing request:: '->'Handling submission:: ', 'Committing request:: '->'Applying agreed submission:: ', 'Exception thrown by downstream processor, unable to continue.'->'Downstream stage failed; cannot continue.', ' exited loop!'->' loop terminated' (tree-wide, so the failure-path lines do not become the only differently-worded ones), 'CommitProcWork'->'StageWork' (thread tags), 'Client session timed out, have not heard from server in '->'Session inactive - no server traffic for ' (the client-visible observable), plus two CommitProcessor-embedding literals. The anonymized tree REBUILT (ant jar) and re-reproduced: the failure is identical (plain create OK, create-with-Stat ConnectionLoss, node absent, pipeline halted, collateral client fails). logs/repro.log = 18991 lines (Log A); logs/symptom.log = 8072681 lines / 1.5GB (Log B) = Log A merged into the shared production log with the SAME map applied to the production stream - necessary because the real production noise mentions CommitProcessor 5.5M times, FinalRequestProcessor 2.6M and FollowerRequestProcessor 350k, which would otherwise re-expose every renamed name and leave the reproduction as the only differently-worded lines. The shared production log is read-only and untouched. Verification (case-insensitive, over source/ + both logs incl. the whole 1.5GB): bug id, create2, the seven original type names and the original log literals all ZERO hits. REDONE 2026-08-12 under the updated M5 specification (context/METHODOLOGY.md commits 466a79e/ebba23d/8d90c20: symptom.md = bare observable + log pointer, never the JIRA-case narrative). The previous symptom.md violated every clause of the new must-NOT list - it named the failing overload create(path,data,acl,mode,Stat), gave the trigger and the mechanism timeline ('from that moment on that follower answers nothing'), and carried the narrowing comparison 'a plain create on the very same connection had succeeded 8 ms earlier', which hands the LLM the discriminating experiment. It is replaced by the exception form: two sentences of observable (client calls stop completing and fail with KeeperException.ConnectionLoss) + the log pointer + the exact client-side line pasted verbatim from logs/symptom.log ('Client session timed out, have not heard from server in 6670ms for sessionid 0x..., closing socket connection and attempting reconnect', confirmed present in the log). No trigger, no failing operation/overload, no mechanism, no at-fault component/class/branch, no what-stays-correct comparison, no text taken from the JIRA ticket. Verification gate re-run: 0 hits for ZOOKEEPER-1851 / bare 1851 / create2 / Create2 across source/, logs/symptom.log and symptom.md; the renamed term createExt appears only in source/ and the log (never in symptom.md, since it is not the observable surface). private/ground_truth.md is unchanged (M5 step 2 is unchanged): both primary sites plus the PASS rule. All post-M5 artifacts (diagnosis/run_1..5.md, the grade JSONs, summary.md) were deleted and M6-M8 reset to PENDING.

RE-RUN against the rewritten (bare-observable) symptom.md. 5 independent single-turn diagnoses, model claude-opus-4-7 effort high, egress iptables-locked to api.anthropic.com:443 (--add-host pins the IP), Bash/Write/Edit/WebFetch/WebSearch/Task/NotebookEdit denied, --safe-mode --no-session-persistence --exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections, no follow-up prompts, throwaway staging dir /tmp/clods-diag-Fp3J holding ONLY source/ + logs/symptom.log + symptom.md. As before, the clods-eval image's baked-in /opt/clods/run_diagnosis.sh is stale, so the tracked context/run_diagnosis.sh was mounted read-only and executed instead (context/ and the image unmodified). This batch ran clean: all 5 runs completed on the first attempt, every stderr empty, no auth interruption. The prompt now embeds only the two-sentence observable + the pasted client-side timeout line, so each run had to locate the failing operation in the log by itself.

4/5 PASS under the stricter symptom. Runs 1, 3, 4 and 5 each named BOTH required root-causing sites with their exact branch conditions - the missing 'case OpCode.createExt:' in FollowerRequestProcessor.run's forward-to-leader switch (createExt matches no label, so zks.getFollower().request() never runs and no proposal/commit can return) AND its absence from CommitProcessor.needCommit (default: return false, so run()'s 'if (needCommit(request)) nextPending.set(...) else sendToNextProcessor(...)' takes the else arm and delivers a hdr==null request to FinalRequestProcessor) - and all four prescribed the fix at both lines. Each had to find the createExt request unaided: symptom.md no longer names the operation, so every run located it in the log via the 'zxid:0xfffffffffffffffe / txntype:unknown' fingerprint and the absent 'Committing request' line. Run 2 FAILED: it names only CommitProcessor.needCommit, mentions FollowerRequestProcessor exactly once and only as the component still enqueuing into the halted processor, never identifies the forwarding switch or its missing case, and prescribes a single-line fix. Its causal account is also wrong - it explains the null header as a timing race ('before the leader's Leader.COMMIT packet has installed the TxnHeader'), which presumes the request reached the leader; it never did. That fix would leave the member dark, stalling in nextPending instead of crashing. No partial credit -> FAIL.

4/5 PASS under the updated M5 symptom specification (unchanged headline score from the superseded narrative-symptom run, but a different failing run: run 2 here, run 3 before). Runs 1, 3, 4, 5 named both required sites with their branch conditions and prescribed the upstream fix at both lines, having first had to locate the failing operation themselves - symptom.md now gives only a ConnectionLoss timeout line, so each run worked backwards from the client timeout to the one request carrying the unset-zxid sentinel with no preceding 'Committing request' line. Run 2 stopped at the first switch that explains the NPE (needCommit), never identified the forwarding switch, and invented a timing race with a leader COMMIT that could never arrive; its one-line fix would convert the crash into a hang. summary.md records both caveats: the DEBUG log prints request type + zxid at every processor hop (a well-signposted search), and the rename removes ticket recognition but not the model's general familiarity with the ZooKeeper wire protocol (run 3 glossed createExt as 'create2, OpCode = 15'; run 2 guessed wrongly that it was the TTL/container create).
